title: After you file
subject: Money

text: Filing is not the end. You wait, you check, and you keep the papers.
Keep the return and the forms for at least three years. That is the usual window for a refund claim or an IRS question.
Where's My Refund on IRS.gov is the official tracker. Direct deposit is faster than a check.
If you claimed the EITC or the Additional Child Tax Credit, do not expect a refund before mid-February.
Pay by the April due date even if you extend the filing. IRS.gov/Payments takes a bank account, card, or a plan.
A payment plan is interest and a fee. It is still better than ignoring a balance.
File an amended return on Form 1040-X if you left out a W-2 or claimed the wrong credit.
If you never filed and you are due a refund, you generally have three years from the original due date to claim it.
You filed, claimed the EITC, and it is January 28. The refund has not arrived. What is true?

choices.label: EITC refunds are held until mid-February. Check Where's My Refund.
The IRS lost it. File again today.
A refund with the EITC arrives in three days.

text: Track it on Where's My Refund. Pay a balance by April. Amend if you were wrong.
Keep the papers three years. This course is a map, not a preparer.

notes: Example course. Tax year 2025 figures, filed in 2026. Confirm on IRS.gov. Not tax advice.
